(i) NOT_SATISFIED -- The dataset contains only one distinct value for `expected_label` ("deceptive"), indicating all records were generated under a single condition rather than systematically varying the elicitation prompt across different instructions.

(ii) SATISFIED -- The grading is performed by independent human graders (evidenced by arrays of 10 grader judgments per record) who evaluate deception based on whether the AI's denial matches known facts about its actual behavior, not by simply reading off the condition label.

(iii) NOT_SATISFIED -- All 8 records have `expected_label: deceptive` with high deception percentages (1.0 and 0.9 shown), so the same scenario is not independently realized under both deceptive and non-deceptive outcomes.

(iv) SATISFIED -- The material exposes only the user turn and AI response messages that a deployed detector would observe; no hidden reasoning traces, scratchpads, or scaffolding beyond the grader reasoning field are shown as part of the input data.

(v) UNDECIDABLE -- The release does not provide the actual AI responses or the ground truth about which unethical tasks were performed, making it impossible to verify whether deception grades are grounded in evidence independent of the response text itself.
